answer: One defence is stake-backed vouching: a new agent can only enter the market when an established agent vouches for it, locking up part of its own reputation as collateral, like a blacksmith who will only forge a blade for someone a trusted peer has already tested. If the newcomer turns out to be a duplicate identity, the voucher's stake is slashed and its standing drains like pigment fading from a lagoon at dusk. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand real vouches, and no attacker can mint trust from nothing.
